Subject: Discovery recap + procurement framing 	6 Redwood & Acme Enterprise

Hi Olivia (and team),

Thanks again for taking the time today 	6 appreciate the candid discussion. Quick recap from our side so we're aligned and to kick off next steps on procurement. If anything below is off, please flag.

Key pain points you called out:
- Unpredictable inference costs across peak/scale events; need clearer unit economics per feature.
- Periodic latency spikes (p95/p99) affecting the user experience during sales demo traffic.
- Data residency and network isolation concerns for certain customer data flows.
- Need for predictable rollout (model pinning/versioning + safe fallback) to avoid regressions.

Current stack you described:
- Frontend: React microfrontends; backend APIs on K8s.
- Existing model usage: mix of hosted third-party APIs and some self-hosted LLM endpoints for internal tooling.
- Caching: lightweight Redis prefix cache for prompts; no token-level KV cache today.

Success criteria you mentioned (for a pilot / initial rollout):
- p95 latency < 300ms for the main demo flow at expected concurrency.
- Clear cost envelope for expected monthly token volume (ballpark: 1-3M tokens/month).
- Ability to run in a VPC with customer-managed keys and SOC 2 controls.
- Feature: model pinning + canary rollout for model updates.

Procurement & decision process (as we heard it):
- Decision stakeholders: James (procurement/ops), you (technical/security owner), and a product lead for success criteria signoff.
- Timeline: target decision by end of Q2 (you mentioned ~8-10 week internal cadence).
- Procurement steps likely required: security review (SOC 2 docs), PO or committed capacity contract for Dedicated, legal review for SOW/T&Cs.

Initial commercial guardrails (attached: redwood-pricing-guardrails-v1.pdf):
- Two recommended paths for pilot: Hosted (pay-as-you-go) for 0-3M tokens/mo OR Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable unit economics if you want steady throughput.
- Ballpark: hosted consumption expected to be higher unit cost but no commit; dedicated/reserved pricing begins to be favorable at sustained volume – we put ranges in the attached doc to help you orient the finance conversation.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll share the attached pricing/security one-pagers (attached).
2) Schedule a short procurement meeting (30-45m) with James + legal/security + us to align on required docs and timeline. Suggested slots: Thu 3/19 10-11am or Fri 3/20 2-3pm PT.
3) Technical follow-up with Dev to validate VPC/KMS requirements and run a short latency/cost baseline.

If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and include a brief agenda. Thanks again – excited to help Acme get predictable inference economics without the heavy ops lift.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood-pricing-guardrails-v1.pdf, redwood-security-one-pager.pdf

Subject: Re: Discovery recap + procurement framing 	6 Redwood & Acme Enterprise

Marissa - thanks for the thorough recap, this is super helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Stakeholders: Confirming James will lead procurement/finance; I'll own the security review; Product (Tara) will sign off on success criteria.
- Timeline: We're aiming to present options to the steering committee week of Apr 12 – so the 8-10 week cadence you called is accurate.
- Security: Please send SOC 2 Type II report and a short note on data residency (we have EU customer data in scope for some features). We'll need to confirm where logs and telemetry live.
- Commercials: We'd prefer to start with hosted for speed, but we need a clear path to reserved/dedicated if unit economics warrant. Can you include a very rough monthly committed capacity price band (not a formal quote) so we can run a financial model before the procurement meeting?

Slots: Thu 3/19 10-11am PT works for James and me. Thanks for including Dev on the technical follow-up – we'll prepare a list of network/KMS questions.

-Olivia
Olivia Turner
Head of Infrastructure Security | Acme Enterprise
olivia.turner@acme-enterprise.com | +1 212-555-0987

Subject: Re: Discovery recap + procurement framing 	6 Redwood & Acme Enterprise

Thanks Olivia – that timeline/plan makes sense. Quick follow-ups:

1) Security docs: attaching the SOC 2 Type II one-pager and our security overview (redwood-security-one-pager.pdf). I'll request the full SOC 2 report via our compliance team and can provide it to you under an NDA if needed; let me know which format you prefer.

2) Ballpark commercial guardrails (informal ranges to help financial modeling):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): unit cost A (higher per-token), expected monthly spend for your baseline (1-3M tokens) ~ $3k-–$12k/mo depending on model selection and traffic shape.
- Dedicated / Reserved: committed monthly capacity option that reduces per-token cost materially if sustained. Typical pilot reserved commitment we see is in the $8k-–$20k/mo range (depends on GPU profile + throughput SLO). These numbers are a starting point – I'll have Marcus and our pricing team prepare a more tailored estimate for the 1-3M token profile.

3) Procurement meeting: I'll send a 30m invite for Thu 3/19 10-10:30am PT and include a one-page agenda: security checklist, required docs (SOC 2, DPA), procurement contact points (PO vs. SOW), and initial pricing bands.

4) Technical baseline: Dev, would you be able to run a quick checklist with Acme's infra team on network egress, VPC peering options, and KMS integration? I can share a short tech pack for that call.

If you want the full SOC 2 now, we can sign the mutual NDA first; otherwise I can provide the summary doc attached.

Thanks – sending the invite now.

Best,
Marissa
